briefs.source_chain: Dealers were short puts/OTM puts after Thursday's record CBOE put day -> Monday's vol crush (VIX 28->20 over ~2.5 sessions) forced dealer buybacks via vanna (puts losing delta twice) plus call delta-buying -> mechanical 84%-advancer melt-up -> on Tuesday the vol crush stalls just as hot October CPI confirms the hike condition Waller floated in his Tuesday-morning speech -> rally stalls, Dec 50bp-hike odds rise to 14% -> record options volume, leveraged-ETF/vol-control dynamics and record VVIX realized vol stack into a powder keg -> McElligott expects a wider outcome distribution and a structurally higher VIX floor tied to AI-capex doubts.
briefs.brief_chain: Monday's 84%-advancer rally was mechanically driven by a vol crush (dealers short puts/OTM puts, vanna-forced buybacks, call delta-buying) -> on Tuesday the vol meltdown stalls, stalling the rally, just as hot October CPI (0.4% MoM, core 0.3% vs 0.2%) confirms the condition Waller floated in a Monday speech -> Dec 50bp-hike odds rise to 14% -> record options volumes, leveraged-ETF rebalancing and reduced vol-control allocation form a powder keg, with VVIX realized vol at a record above 2018 Volmageddon -> McElligott expects a wider outcome distribution and a structurally higher VIX floor tied to AI-capex doubts.

distortions.what: Brief says Waller floated the 50bp-hike condition "in a Monday speech"; source has Waller's London speech happening "this morning" — Tuesday, the same morning as the note and hours before the same-day CPI print. Searched "Waller" (all 3 occurrences) and "this morning"/"Tuesday" around it; no Monday speech reference exists in the source.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the causal chain (Waller floats the condition, hot CPI confirms it, hike odds jump to 14%) is unchanged regardless of which day the speech fell on; no stance, trade/instrument, conviction level or invalidation condition changes.

briefs.source_chain: Wilson turned negative on semis in June on extreme earnings-revisions breadth -> Thursday's 4.4% plunge closed the index/breadth gap to 2% -> correction enters its final phase, needing one more marginal low into 7,100-7,300 on lower momentum as a classic retest -> that sets up a year-end rally into 2027, so add quality cyclicals and Industrials now -> the flagged risk (a more-hawkish-than-expected Fed echoing 2018) materialized a day later when Waller's 25bp-lean/50bp-on-the-table comment was followed by hot core CPI, pricing a December hike with 14% odds of 50bp -> the piece's own view is that this makes Wilson's risk case (drawn-out bottom bleeding into December) more likely than his base case, citing CTAs modeled as sellers in every scenario this week.
briefs.brief_chain: Wilson, negative on semis since June on extreme earnings-revisions breadth, says the correction (breadth gap closed to 2% after Thursday's 4.4% plunge) is entering its final phase: a marginal new low into 7,100-7,300 on lower momentum completes a classic retest, setting up a year-end rally into 2027, so he recommends adding quality cyclicals and Industrials -> the main risk is a more-hawkish-than-expected Fed echoing 2018 -> that risk showed up a day later as Waller's 25bp-lean/50bp-on-the-table comment was followed by hot core CPI, pricing a December hike at 14% odds of 50bp -> the article's own view is that this makes Wilson's risk case more likely than his base case, since CTAs are modeled as sellers in every scenario this week.

briefs.source_chain: The author expected a Monday low but was wrong — buying overwhelmed the last systematic seller, Risk Control, instead -> Risk Control exposure at 55% (1st pctile vs 1Y), matching only two prior washouts (Aug 2024, Apr 2025) that preceded +17%/+24% SPX gains over 4 months -> CTA equity exposure is negative at -5%, a bottoming signal when real money isn't selling -> the downside feedback loop is largely removed since systematic funds won't amplify discretionary selling, and retail/foreign/buyback demand keeps selloffs shallow -> intraday buying is heavy across S&P, Nasdaq and leveraged ETFs while CTAs have barely bought but hold higher triggers -> desk expects SPX to grind +10%+ higher over 3 months.
briefs.brief_chain: The systematic-selling washout is complete: Risk Control, the last remaining seller, was overwhelmed by buying today instead of producing the expected Monday low -> Risk Control exposure at 55% (1st pctile vs 1Y), the lowest since the tariff shock, with the only two comparable washouts followed by +17%/+24% SPX gains over 4 months -> CTA exposure negative at -5%, a bottoming signal when real money isn't selling -> the downside feedback loop is largely removed, so retail/foreign ETF buyers/returning buybacks keep news-driven selloffs shallow -> intraday S&P/Nasdaq buying plus $24bn leveraged-ETF buying, with CTAs barely bought but holding higher triggers -> desk expects SPX to grind at least +10% higher over 3 months.

briefs.source_chain: Three capitulation signals trigger together (record -$365bn Excess Flow, RMM buying the dip at 68th pctile after the largest selling episode since Covid, VIX Cross-Asset Rank at 96%) -> together these imply forced selling/oversold conditions, so UBS expects a Monday low as systematic/hedge-fund unwind pressure fades -> three systematic strategies sold $170-210bn today (Risk Control, Lev ETFs, CTA), with another $200-270bn of Risk Control selling expected over two days before both flows shrink sharply after Monday -> PB net leverage (18th pctile) and L/S ratio (8th pctile) are very low, so short-squeeze risk is elevated -> investor conversations aren't panicked, with clients waiting to buy weakness rather than capitulating -> a fourth test (VIX/SPX intraday hi-lo ratio) is not met since SPX is only -5.9% from peak vs. the ~-9.5% usually needed.
